c74object.name: mqtt.midi
c74object.description: Sends and receives MIDI over MQTT, as raw MIDI bytes and through a virtual MIDI port.

discussion.p: Each MQTT message carries one or more complete MIDI messages, as defined by the MIDI 1.0 specification: status and data bytes, SysEx from F0 to F7, real-time bytes such as clock (F8). Running status is allowed. Payloads with missing, stray or undefined bytes are ignored.

receive is the topic filter MIDI arrives on; wildcards are allowed, e.g. studio/+/midi for every device. send is the topic MIDI is published to. Messages on the object's own send topic are not received back.

The inlet and the left outlet carry raw MIDI bytes, like midiout and midiin: use midiformat and midiparse. With port, received messages also play on a virtual MIDI port that Max patches and other applications can open, and MIDI sent to the port is published on send. Virtual ports are available on macOS.
MIDI is published at QoS 0 and never retained.

objarg.name: client
objarg.digest: Name of the mqtt.client to use

method.name: int
method.description: Raw MIDI bytes, as midiout takes them, including running status, real-time bytes and SysEx. Each complete message is published.

method.name: list
method.description: A list of raw MIDI bytes.

attribute.name: receive
attribute.description: The topic filter to receive MIDI from. Empty to receive nothing.

attribute.name: send
attribute.description: The topic to publish MIDI to, without wildcards. Empty to send nothing.

attribute.name: port
attribute.description: Name of a virtual MIDI port to create. Empty for none.

entry.name: left outlet
entry.description: Received MIDI as raw bytes, one int at a time, as midiin outputs them.

entry.name: middle outlet
entry.description: port with the port name, once Max lists the virtual port as an input and an output device. Connect it to ctlin, notein, ctlout and other MIDI objects: they look up their port when they are created, which in the same patch is before the port exists.
